title: Protest in Abdanan following fatal bus crash
seoTitle: Abdanan protest over fatal bus crash

tea.why: Protesters are demonstrating against the deaths of 13 people in a bus crash, citing state incompetence and poor road safety.
tea.want: Participants are demanding the resignation of officials and accountability for those responsible for the fatal accident.
tea.changed: Nov 17: Protesters continued demonstrations into the evening, with reports of slogans directed against state leadership.

summary: Hundreds of people gathered in Vali-e Asr Square in Abdanan, Ilam Province, on Tuesday to protest a bus crash that killed 13 people. According to the Fars news agency, the crowd grew from an initial 200–300 participants to approximately 1,000. While initial chants focused on the accident and calls for resignations, reports indicate that slogans later shifted to include political themes. The Abdanan prosecutor, Amrollah Misaie, stated that authorities would investigate the incident and hold those at fault accountable, while warning against actions that disrupt public order. Separately, the Abdanan Security Council urged citizens to remain calm. Some reports noted that families of the victims requested that no gatherings be held in their name, while other accounts described protesters tearing down banners of state institutions.
response: The Abdanan public and revolutionary prosecutor warned of a firm response to those disrupting public order. The Abdanan Security Council called on citizens to remain calm and avoid unlawful actions.

updates.text: A protest began in Vali-e Asr Square in Abdanan, with participants growing to approximately 1,000 people.
The Abdanan prosecutor warned that individuals disrupting public order would be dealt with firmly.
Euronews reported that the protest continued into the evening and included anti-regime slogans.
